### Added
- **A pinned server can receive the person's ID token next to its grant.** A server that acts for the person on two systems needs two of their credentials -- the grant of its pinned authorization server (a GitHub App user token, say) and the person's own identity for calls back through muster -- but an `MCPServer` carried one: `forwardToken` is rejected next to `authorizationServer`, so such a server was registered twice. `spec.auth.forwardIdentity: true`, valid only with `type: oauth` and an `authorizationServer` pin (CEL rule, and the same check in filesystem mode and `core_mcpserver_validate`), sends the session's upstream ID token -- the token `forwardToken` would put in `Authorization`, read on every request so a refreshed one is used -- in the `X-Muster-Id-Token` header; `Authorization` keeps the pinned grant. A session without an upstream ID token sends no header, a server without the field never receives it, the server's `requiredAudiences` are requested at login as for a `forwardToken` server, and a change of the field resets the sessions' connections. As with `forwardToken`, the forwarded token is not audience-scoped to the server. `muster create mcpserver` gained `--forward-identity`. ([#1317](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1317))
